screening_decisions.reason: RCT in women with stress urinary incontinence. One arm received pelvic floor muscle (PFM) exercises via digital palpation, another received PFM exercises via biofeedback, and the control group had no exercises (no treatment). Meets all criteria.
RCT in women with SUI. The app treatment arm is based on PFMT; the control group received postponed treatment (wait-list/inactive control). Meets criteria.
RCT in postmenopausal women with SUI. Three arms: control (no treatment), PFME alone, PFME+biofeedback. One arm is PFMT and another is an inactive control (no treatment). Meets criteria.

RCT in women with urge or mixed (urge-predominant) incontinence. The biofeedback-assisted behavioral treatment arm includes pelvic floor muscle training as part of behavioral therapy; compared to placebo control (inactive). Meets criteria, though PFMT component not explicitly detailed in abstract but standard for such behavioural programs.
RCT in older women with stress incontinence. Three arms: pelvic muscle exercise (PFMT), biofeedback, and control (no treatment). PFMT vs inactive control present.
RCT in women with genuine stress incontinence. One arm is pelvic floor exercises (PFMT) and another is untreated control (no treatment). Meets criteria.
RCT in women with SUI. Intervention group performed perineal (pelvic floor) exercises; control group received no treatment. PFMT vs inactive control.
RCT in women with SUI. One arm is pelvic floor exercises (PFMT) and another is untreated control (no treatment). Meets criteria.
RCT in women with stress and mixed UI. PFMT group vs control (no treatment). Meets criteria.

RCT in women with UI. The BMP includes pelvic floor muscle training (as indicated by assessment of pelvic muscle strength). Control group received no treatment. Meets criteria, though BMP description in abstract is limited.
Abstract does not mention a no-treatment or inactive control arm. It compares medical gymnastics and electrical stimulation, both active treatments. No PFMT vs inactive control.

RCT in elderly women with SUI. Intervention includes pelvic floor muscle and fitness exercises; control group received no exercise (inactive control in initial phase). PFMT vs inactive control present.
RCT in women with stress, urge and mixed UI. Exercise arms include pelvic floor muscle training; the education-only group serves as inactive control. Meets criteria.
RCT in women with SUI, UUI, MUI. Multidimensional exercise includes PFMT; control group received no treatment. Meets criteria.

RCT in older women with stress/urge/mixed UI. Intervention includes PFMT with manual palpation and behavioural therapy; control group received advice/pamphlet only (inactive/minimal intervention). Meets criteria.
RCT in women with SUI. PFMT group received supervised physiotherapy; control group received no treatment. PFMT vs inactive control.
RCT in women with mild SUI. Intervention teaches 'The Knack' (timed pelvic floor muscle contraction before/during cough), which is a PFMT technique; wait-listed control group. Meets criteria.
RCT in women with SUI. Two PFMT arms (individual, group) and a control group with no treatment. PFMT vs inactive control.
RCT in women with MUI. One arm is PFMT; waiting list control group (inactive). Meets criteria.
RCT in postmenopausal women with UI. The physical therapy arm includes PFMT; control group received osteoporosis education (inactive). Meets criteria.
RCT in women with UI. Pelvic muscle exercise (PFMT) group and a control group (no treatment) were included. PFMT vs inactive control present.
RCT in women with SUI. G2: kinesitherapy (PFMT) alone; G3: control (no treatment). PFMT vs inactive control present.
RCT in female athletes with stress UI. Intervention group received PFMT (pelvic floor muscles rehabilitation program); control group received only a pamphlet (inactive). Meets criteria.
RCT in women with genuine stress incontinence. One arm is pelvic floor exercises (PFMT); control group had no treatment. Meets criteria.
RCT in women with stress incontinence. Treatment group received pelvic floor exercises (PFMT); control group received no therapy. Meets criteria.
RCT in women with stress or mixed UI. PFMT group vs control (no contact, no treatment). Meets criteria.

This is a trial comparing a care model (nurse specialist involvement) versus usual care; it does not have a specific arm testing PFMT against an inactive control. Does not meet the intervention/comparator criteria.
This is a secondary analysis of satisfaction, not an RCT evaluating PFMT vs an inactive control. Excluded.

RCT comparing two active behavioral trainings (with/without biofeedback) against a self-help booklet (an active, minimal behavioural treatment), not a clearly inactive control such as no treatment or placebo.

This is a feasibility study, not a definitive RCT, and the abstract does not describe a clearly randomised design (volunteers assigned to groups). Does not meet the study design criterion with certainty.
RCT comparing two active PFMT arms (supervised vs unsupervised); no no-treatment, placebo, sham or inactive control arm. Excluded.
RCT in women with LBP and UI. Both groups received active treatment (routine physiotherapy in control, plus stabilization exercises in intervention). No inactive control arm.
Three arms: behavioural training, behavioural training+PFES, and a self-help booklet (active minimal treatment). No truly inactive (no treatment/placebo) control. Excluded.
RCT in elderly women with UI. Training group received Kegel's exercises (PFMT) plus other exercises; control group presumably usual care/no treatment. Meets criteria.

RCT in women with UI. Behavioural therapy (which typically includes PFMT as a core component) versus no therapy control group. PFMT vs inactive control present, though abstract does not itemize interventions.

Economic evaluation alongside a two-arm PFMT trial (internet vs postal). The RCT lacked a concurrent no-treatment arm; it used baseline as a no-treatment comparator, which does not satisfy the comparator criterion.
RCT comparing two active PFMT delivery methods (internet vs postal); no inactive control arm. Excluded.
Follow-up of the two-arm PFMT trial (internet vs postal); no inactive control. Excluded.
RCT in women with SUI. Exercise group performed co-contraction of TA and PFM (PFMT); control group (no treatment). Meets criteria.

RCT (pilot) in frail older women with UI. Intervention includes behavioural UI treatments (including PFMT) combined with physical activity; control group likely usual care/no treatment. Meets criteria.
Population is gynaecologic cancer survivors with 'pelvic floor dysfunction', not specifically diagnosed with SUI, UUI, or MUI. Not clearly meeting the population criterion.
